text:
maya: heads-up — main is red right after my merge (PR #8421, refactor/cache-shim). smoke-gpu failed during the serve-smoke step. not sure it's my change but pinging first responders.
ben: on it. can you paste the failing log snippet?
maya: sure — from the smoke job:```
E 00:12:03 serve_smoke.py:47 AssertionError: expected 0 errors, got 3
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/workspace/serve_smoke.py", line 47, in <module>
    assert total_errors == 0
AssertionError
  -- gpu-utils: cudnn runtime error: out of memory while allocating KV cache
```
oworkaround: it's intermittent but reproduced in this run. link: https://ci.redwood.dev/runs/1790000119
own: @maya did you merge a change touching the KV cache or batching config?
maya: I only renamed a helper and moved a redis-prefetch call. didn't change batch sizes or quant configs.
ben: ok starting a rerun of the smoke-gpu job: `ci-retry --run 1790000119 --job serve-smoke-gpu`
ci-bot: rerun requested by ben for run 1790000119 — new run 1790000205 queued :arrows_clockwise:
ben: giving it a minute. if rerun passes we can label as flaky, if it fails again we should bisect or revert.
own: if it's OOM in KV cache, might be a kernel/alloc regression. @sre-oncall can you check node-level OOMs?
sre-oncall: looking now — pulling logs from node gpu-12: `kubectl -n prod logs pod/serve-smoke-679f -c runner`
sre-oncall: found repeated "cudaMalloc failed: out of memory" entries, plus one segfault at the end. saving full dump to /tmp/ci-dumps/1790000205.log
lucy: @maya can you confirm the PR ran smoke locally? any skipped tests?
maya: yeah ran smoke locally on my dev rig (A100-ish) and it passed, so odd that CI hit OOM. I didn't skip anything.
ben: rerun just finished and it's red again, same error. marking as blocker.
ben: plan: (1) start bisect to find merge that introduced alloc change, (2) grab full docker image + reproduce, (3) if bisect points to recent change, revert. who can take bisect?
own: I can kick off a quick bisect across the last 6 merges. doing `ci-bisect --branch main --since 6 --job serve-smoke-gpu` now.
own: bisect started — will post culprit when done. ETA ~12-15m.
ci-bot: bisect job launched by owen: bisect-1790000210 — progress updates will post to this thread.
ben: thanks. @maya if we find your change implicated, we may need a small revert while investigating. please stand by.
maya: understood — happy to help debug if it's tied to my helper move.
own: quick interim check — kernel bump from 5.18 -> 5.19 was rolled into infra merge 1789999990 last night. that could affect GPU drivers.
sre-oncall: confirmed kernel 5.19 nodes are in the pool since 03:20 UTC. rolling nodes back is nontrivial during traffic.
ben: good find. owen, include infra merge in bisect scope.
own: will do. bisect log shows failure repro at commit 179/infra/rollup (candidate), isolating now.
own: bisect result: commit 1790000057 (infra: kernel bump + nvidia-driver update) reproduces OOM.
ben: that matches node change. not a code regression. tagging infra and paging oncall infra.
ben: @sre-oncall can we temporarily route smoke jobs to legacy kernel pool as a hotfix?
sre-oncall: yes, can gate the smoke job label to `kernel-5.18` nodes for CI — will patch the CI runner group and requeue.
ci-bot: CI config patch merged by sre-oncall, requeueing smoke-gpu on kernel-5.18 nodes — new run 1790000288
ben: re-run succeeded on 5.18 pool. marking main as green and unlinking blocker. :white_check_mark:
maya: whew. thanks everyone. follow-up: I'll open an issue to coordinate with infra on driver/kernel compatibility and add a CI matrix check so we catch this before merges.
own: filing issue now: https://issues.redwood.dev/INFRA-431 — assign infra\/kernel team.
ben: closing loop — owner for immediate triage = owen (bisect), hotfix = sre-oncall (node gate), follow-up = maya (issue + test). I'll add notes to the merge PR.
lucy: nice teamwork :clap:
ben: thanks — moving to postmortem if infra wants one.
ci-bot: thread archived after resolution.
